validationBoundary: Windows isolated Release development build and existing console Core/offscreen WPF runners; no release or packaging.
Comparison is against the preceding continuation round, not a pristine HEAD baseline.
All previous registrations retained; two opt-in native-audio checks and manual desktop play were not run.
Failure errors retain 1200 characters with explicit truncation; timing tables retain the slowest 20.
Official content/portrait evidence is static; gameplay evidence comes from accepted commands and cold replay checks.

genderEvidence.basis: Historical identity and the visually inspected official portrait. Male is an inference, not an explicit current API gender field.

newSharedCapabilities: A mandatory single owner TurnEnding operation privately offers the actual turn participant a draw and a frozen whole-hand exchange, including the self draw branch.
Exact owner lost-HP HE selection is an explicit nullable opt-in; it rejects an insufficient initial payment and retains the old shrinking selection contract.
Named bound-card target counts preserve the paid quantity across native movement/recovery children and support zero through the frozen maximum targets.
SupportRecovery AI scores all legal target subsets including the empty set using public HP and tactical relations.
Selected effective suits can be explicitly frozen on the exact private cost binding, with a defensive read-only copy and strict aligned producer invariants; legacy suit branches remain unchanged.
Only the newly introduced current-turn exchange operation retains an actual own-ending hand-count fact, preserving previously accepted own trigger frame shapes.
newBehaviorCoverage: Actual ol:junbing lets the current foreign turn participant choose, draws once, gifts its whole actual hand and returns exact frozen quantities through real movement children.
Actual owner-end use retains the original one-card hand-count fact across eligibility, its private prompt and cold replay; accept only draws and decline preserves entities.
A real obtained-card child adds owner inventory without enlarging the original return debt; a real SilverLion return opens a genuine HP-recovery child once.
Native AI can accept as the current participant or privately select the owner return, with preserved original invoices and no repeated paid stage after cold replay.
A genuine gift child can exhaust all transferable HE resources; a zero-entity return retains the original two-card gift invoice and completes without creating later debt.
More than eight real HE candidates remain private; two chosen cards pay in one atomic movement batch and real armor recovery does not change the named two-target cap.
An extra one-card binding does not replace the named paid-count source; selected self and other recipients resume through native recovery children once.
Insufficient exact costs, premature finishes, wrong actors, stale choices and second same-phase activations reject without changing command state or quota.
Single and multiple effective spade-to-heart costs freeze consistently and cause no black fee; genuine spade costs lose one HP; frozen suit collections reject mutation.
Actual registered ol:quji completes a two-card black cost, a zero-target choice and one real owner HP loss, then rejects another same-phase activation.
A positive-reward shared fixture activates through native AI advancement, pays its own cards privately and chooses a real named target subset; all-full public target scoring chooses empty.
coverageLimitations: Manual desktop gameplay and current official-client or cross-skill FAQ acceptance were not performed.
Self, zero and full-HP Quji recipients follow the documented interpretation of current text; historical official recipient commentary conflicts with that text.
The shortage return and pre-discard effective-suit rules are explicit engine interpretations, not verified official Quji/Hongyan rulings.
Native AI activation uses a shared fixture with a genuine eight-card draw tail, while actual Quji commands use unchanged registered content; this does not establish actual Quji tactical quality.
Failure comparisons use saved names and first error prefixes capped at 1200 characters, rather than claiming identical complete stack traces.
The measured routine scope remains above the approximately one-minute target; no retained registrations were removed.
